label: Efficiency, cardiac output and arterial O2 lie in the measured teleost ranges
statement_en: eta <= 0.15, oxycaloric <= 19.35 J/ml, cardiac output <= 0.075 ml/s and arterial O2 <= 0.21 ml/ml imply an aerobic ceiling of at most 0.0458 W.

hypotheses.name: Delphi.Empirical.TeleostAerobic
hypotheses.statement: eta <= 0.15, oxycaloric <= 19.35 J/ml, cardiac output <= 0.075 ml/s and arterial O2 <= 0.21 ml/ml imply an aerobic ceiling of at most 0.0458 W.

from.efficiency: efficiency: { value: 0.15, kind: 'proxy', species: 'Salmo salar (ventricular muscle)', source: 'gamperl2021: efficiency of ventricular muscle ~15% in salmon (7% in char); trout ventricle 15-25% (Harwood et al. 2002, cited there). No fetched value for fish skeletal muscle, so cardiac muscle is used.'
from.oxycaloric: oxycalorific_J_per_mgO2: { value: 13.54, kind: 'secondary', source: 'gerry2014 (Fig. 1 legend): "oxycaloric value of 13.54 J mg-1 O2" citing their ref. 89' }
from.cardiacRange: Q_range_ml_min_kg: { value: [20, 75], kind: 'secondary', species: 'O. mykiss', source: 'gerry2014 Discussion: ventral aortic flow-cuff values ~20 at rest to ~75 ml/min/kg maximum (citing refs)' }
from.haemoglobinCapacity: cap_ml_per_ml: { value: (4 * 0.9 * 22.4) / 1000, kind: 'proxy', species: 'Oncorhynchus mykiss', source: 'derived from rummer2015 Table 1 [Hb] 0.9 mM per tetramer (Hct standardised to ~25%): 4 x 0.9 mmol/l x 22.4 ml/mmol = 0.0806 ml O2/ml' }

hypotheses.source: physiology/muscle.js (efficiency, oxycaloric), physiology/cardiac.js (cardiac output range), physiology/haemoglobin.js (blood O2 capacity), as cited in lean/eliminate/physiology-candidates.json
hypotheses.observation: No teleost in the ranges the physiology chain cites has a sustained aerobic ceiling above 0.0458 W at the measured mass (0.06 kg). This is what makes the C14 eliminations binding: they hold for every animal the measured record allows, not only for one choice of proxies.

mass_kg.note: the cardiac-output ceiling (75 ml/min/kg) was converted to ml/s for a 0.06 kg fish; at any other mass the absolute bound 0.075 ml/s is not the measured one

scope.basis: physiology chain proxies from other teleosts, evaluated for a 0.06 kg fish
scope.note: The bound is an upper bound at one mass, and the cardiac output ceiling is the maximum of a secondary range (20 to 75 ml/min/kg, gerry2014 Discussion). It bounds SUSTAINED AEROBIC power only: burst power on white-muscle stores is outside it, and that is what a flying fish is understood to use. Scaling it to another mass requires the cardiac output per kg, not this number.

cardiacOutput.description: cardiac output of a 0.06 kg fish
